note: Every time you change al-extract.js or al-build.js, rerun all cases, not just one: a change often breaks only one kind of project (while wrapping up 0.3.0, the pseudo-element ordering fix broke only Project C). expected_behavior is the acceptance criteria, judged by a person; baseline is the result of the 0.4.0 one-screen-at-a-time rebuild, not a ceiling. Marquees, carousels and fade-in animations make the diff fluctuate by about 0.3%. When sending to Figma, follow the code-to-figma hard rules: one screen at a time.

evals.project: Project A prototype (Vue 3, SCSS, mobile 360 wide)
evals.query: Bring this prototype's cart state screens into Figma and bind them to the project's design system
expected_behavior: The layout tree picks up Vue components; framework in stats.json is vue3
al-diff median is below 1%
audit-screens.js reports no structural issues
Library icon colors are correct; semi-transparent colors did not become opaque

evals.project: Project B (Vue 3, Tailwind, MSW; desktop 1280, mobile 360, full page)
evals.query: Bring the home page and the promotions page into Figma, including desktop full page and mobile
expected_behavior: Layer names are not Tailwind utility classes
Images are split into separate files for upload; full-page data SVGs are under 2MB; no images are missing
The stacking order of product card images, sheen and badges matches the browser
Progress bar lengths and line-clamp match the browser
Swiper is not made into a component

baseline.note: The marquee content is random data that MSW generates in a service worker, so it differs on every recapture and the L01 and L02 diffs fluctuate. The ticker-content frame offset in the audit comes from the marquee content width; it is a known limitation

evals.project: Project C (Vue 3, SCSS, Playwright fixture mock; desktop 1280)
evals.query: Bring the compact list and full list states of the order history into Figma
expected_behavior: States are set up with the project's e2e fixtures and pages, without changing the repo
The sticky nav bar is above the content
Icons have no black square background; checkboxes have the box and the check mark
The font size of labels with transform: scale() matches the browser
The table header's dark background is intact, table lines are 1px, and the tabs' small triangles and the checkbox check marks look the same as in the browser

evals.project: Project D (Nuxt 4, Tailwind, SCSS, mock upstream; desktop 1920, mobile 360, full page)
evals.query: Bring the home page and the category page into Figma, full page on both desktop and mobile
expected_behavior: Components are captured in dev mode; the repo is unchanged; the .nuxt cache the run created has been cleared
image-set backgrounds and video frames are both present
Scrolling lists have a fixed height and are clipped
When the same component has different layout directions on mobile and desktop, each becomes its own variant
The icon CDN is allowed; stats.json has no empty-icon warning; icon colors match the browser
Truncated product names don't push the price in the same row out of the card; the two footer columns and the description area have no fixed offset
SVG background images are scaled proportionally inside their box, and glows look the same as in the browser

baseline.note: With the CDN allowed, icons actually load, and the vector colors of multicolor icons are not in the tokens (none matches a token exactly), so the binding ratio is lower than 0.3.0's 0.86. L01 was 28.96% and is 0.28% after fixing SVG background image scaling and the drop-shadow glow; Project D does not use mask-image. The swiper-wrapper frame offset in the audit comes from the carousel track width; it is a known limitation

evals.project: Project E (Vue 3, frappe-ui, Tailwind, oklch palette, CSS mask icons; all data comes from backend APIs; desktop 1280, full page)
evals.query: Make a state board of every state of the to-do page: loading, load failed, no permission, and the three roles employee/manager/HR
expected_behavior: States are set up by intercepting backend APIs (the examples/api-intercept approach), without signing in or changing the repo; setup returns different data per card ID, so changing the capture order doesn't change the result
All colors are extracted: backgrounds, borders, badge backgrounds and text colors; the color stats returned by __alBuild are not empty
lucide-* icons are vectors colored with the background color, not solid color blocks
The error state shows the message from the backend, not an "Internal Server Error" filled in by the framework
Text offsets caused by tabular numbers (tabular-nums) are within 8px, and the report explains why

baseline.note: 0.5.0 trial run: all 15 screens were captured and 13 were built in Figma; only the representative screen E01 was compared (1.03%; 2.03% before the fix, when the whole screen had no color). Comparison and audit for the other screens are not done yet because the Figma MCP call limit was reached; fill in diffPercent next time. There is no design system library, so colorBinding does not apply. M01–M03 have 16–31 log.drift entries, concentrated in tabular-nums date badges (about 6px)

evals.project: Project F (React 19, Vite, Radix/shadcn-style Button, Tooltip and DropdownMenu, lucide-react, Tailwind 4 oklch palette; data comes from /api/orders; desktop 1024)
evals.query: Bring the four states of the order list into Figma: with data, empty list, loading, and load failed
expected_behavior: framework in stats.json is react; with a production build it is null and there is a warning
The trigger buttons of Tooltip and DropdownMenu are named Button, not TooltipTrigger or DropdownMenuTrigger; an <a> wrapped by Button asChild is also named Button
OrderRow, Badge, Skeleton, EmptyState and ErrorState are components; lucide icons are vectors named after the icon (RefreshCw, Funnel…)
Layer names contain no auto-generated ids like radix-_r_1_ and no Tailwind classes like inline-flex
Loading is set up with a request that never responds; the error state shows the message from the backend

baseline.note: 0.8.0 (2026-11-14): all four screens built in Figma into state board slots that first held browser screenshots. al-diff: 0.12% (O01), 0.02% (O02, O03, O04), median 0.02%. No text or box drift, every container with data layout is Auto Layout, 13 components (Button x4, Badge x3, OrderRow x2, Skeleton x3, App x4 variants; ErrorState, EmptyState, LoadingRows, 5 icons), 491 nodes, no unused components. No design system, so no colors are bound. audit-screens flagged O04 for icon frames counted as containers; fixed in the same version
